block-definition.comment: Makes a new module and puts it in a variable with the given name. The variable then stands for the module in every other block; its watcher shows the settings. oscillator: produces a tone. Settings: wave (saw, square, triangle or sine), frequency (Hz; 440 is the A above middle C), pulse width (1 to 99 %; the share of each cycle the square wave spends high, 50 is an even square; other waves ignore it), control (a module whose signal bends the frequency, in semitones), trigger (a module whose rising signal restarts the wave). filter: lets the low part of a sound through. Settings: cutoff (Hz; sound above it is cut away), resonance (0 to 100 %; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80; starts at 100), input (the module whose sound is filtered), control (a module whose signal moves the cutoff, in semitones). ADSR: an envelope, a control signal that rises when its gate opens and falls when it closes. Settings: attack (seconds to climb to the peak), decay (seconds to fall to the sustain level), sustain (% of the peak held while the gate is open), release (seconds to fall to zero after the gate closes), amount (the peak: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack), gate (a module whose signal opens the gate, or empty to use the gate block). volume: makes a sound louder or softer. Settings: level (0 to 100 %, the loudness with nothing in control), input (the module whose sound is adjusted), control (a module whose signal adds to the level, in %; an ADSR with amount 100 and level 0 makes notes start and stop). LFO: a slow repeating control signal. Settings: wave (saw, square, triangle or sine, the shape of the motion), speed (cycles per second), amount (the swing each way: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack), trigger (a module whose rising signal restarts the cycle). Amount 1 into an oscillator's control gives vibrato, 50 into a volume's control gives tremolo, 24 into a filter's control gives a wah. delay: repeats a sound as echoes. Settings: time (seconds between echoes), repeats (0 to 95 %, how much each echo feeds the next), blend (0 to 100 %, share of echo in the output), input. noise: white noise as a sound, or random steps as a control signal. Settings: kind (white or random steps), speed (steps per second), amount (the swing: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack, 1 for full noise), trigger (a module whose rising signal picks a new step). ring modulator: multiplies two sounds, giving bell-like tones. Settings: input, input 2. wavefolder: folds the peaks of a sound back on themselves, adding harsh overtones. Settings: fold (0 to 100 %), input. waveform processor: a wavefolder with a control jack, so an envelope or LFO can move the fold. Settings: fold, input, control (adds % to fold). audio divider: a square wave one, two or three octaves below the input. Settings: octaves (1 to 3), input. slew limiter: smooths a control signal, so steps become slides. Settings: rise and fall (seconds), input. trigger divider: passes every n-th gate it receives. Settings: divide by (1 to 16), trigger. trigger sequencer: a repeating pattern of gates. Settings: pattern (text; x is a gate, . is a rest), tempo (steps per minute), clock (a module whose rising signal advances a step; empty to use the tempo). sequencer: a repeating row of notes as a pitch signal. Settings: notes (MIDI note numbers separated by spaces; 69 is A 440, which is 0 at a pitch control), tempo, clock. Plug it into an oscillator's control. Give a sequencer and a trigger sequencer the same clock, such as a square LFO, to keep them in step. The settings are saved with the project. After loading, a module is rebuilt from them the next time a block uses it.

inputs.input: oscillatoroscillator filter ADSR volume LFO delay noise ring modulator wavefolder waveform processor audio divider slew limiter trigger divider trigger sequencer sequencer

block-definition.comment: Changes one setting of an oscillator. Drop the variable holding the oscillator into the first slot. wave: saw, square, triangle or sine frequency: Hz pulse width: 1 to 99 %, the share of each cycle the square wave spends high; 50 is an even square, other waves ignore it control: the name of a module whose signal bends the frequency, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it trigger: the name of a module whose rising signal restarts the wave, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match: a list of waves, a typed number, or a list of modules. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a filter. Drop the variable holding the filter into the first slot. cutoff: Hz; sound above it is cut away resonance: 0 to 100 %; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80 input: the module whose sound is filtered, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it control: the module whose signal moves the cutoff, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of an ADSR envelope. Drop the variable holding the ADSR into the first slot. attack: seconds to climb to the peak decay: seconds to fall to the sustain level sustain: % of the peak held while the gate is open release: seconds to fall to zero after the gate closes amount: the peak; semitones when plugged into a control jack, % when plugged into a level jack gate: the module whose signal opens the gate, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to use the gate block Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.
Opens or closes the gate of an ADSR envelope by hand, like pressing and releasing a key. Opening starts the attack, closing starts the release. Drop the variable holding the ADSR into the first slot.

Changes one setting of a volume module. Drop the variable holding it into the first slot. level: 0 to 100 %, the loudness with nothing in control input: the module whose sound is adjusted, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it control: the module whose signal adds to the level, in %, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it. An ADSR with amount 100 and level 0 makes notes start and stop with its gate. Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of an LFO, a slow repeating control signal. Drop the variable holding it into the first slot. wave: saw, square, triangle or sine, the shape of the motion speed: cycles per second amount: the swing each way; semitones when plugged into a control jack, % when plugged into a level jack trigger: the module whose rising signal restarts the cycle, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a delay, which repeats a sound as echoes. time: seconds between echoes repeats: 0 to 95 %, how much of each echo feeds the next blend: 0 to 100 %, the share of echo in the output input: the module whose sound is echoed Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a noise module. kind: white (a hiss, for sound) or random steps (a stepped random control signal) speed: new random steps per second amount: the swing; semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack; 1 gives full-strength noise as a sound trigger: a module whose rising signal picks a new random step Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a ring modulator, which multiplies two sounds into bell-like tones. input, input 2: the two modules whose sounds are multiplied Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a wavefolder, which folds the peaks of a sound back on themselves. fold: 0 to 100 %, how hard the sound is folded input: the module whose sound is folded Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a waveform processor, a wavefolder whose fold can be moved by another module. fold: 0 to 100 % input: the module whose sound is folded control: a module whose signal adds % to the fold Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of an audio divider, which makes a square wave below the input. octaves: 1, 2 or 3 octaves down input: the module whose sound sets the pitch Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a slew limiter, which smooths a control signal so steps become slides. rise: seconds to glide up fall: seconds to glide down input: the module whose control signal is smoothed Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a trigger divider, which passes every n-th gate. divide by: 1 to 16 trigger: the module whose gates are counted Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a trigger sequencer, a repeating pattern of gates. pattern: text, one character per step; x is a gate, . is a rest tempo: steps per minute, used when no clock is plugged in clock: a module whose rising signal advances one step Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a sequencer, a repeating row of notes sent as a pitch signal. notes: MIDI note numbers separated by spaces; 69 is A 440, which plays an oscillator at its frequency setting tempo: steps per minute, used when no clock is plugged in clock: a module whose rising signal advances one step Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Reports a mix module that adds the sounds of the given modules together. Drop module variables into the slots, or type their names; click the arrows for more slots. Use the result where a module goes, for example in a filter's input or the speaker's input: set speaker input to (mix osc1 osc2)
Plugs a module into the speaker so you hear it. Drop the variable holding the module into the slot. An empty slot unplugs the speaker and silences the synth; the stop sign does the same.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 1) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 4) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.
Copies the settings of an oscillator into the chosen Preset block, replacing what it held. Control and trigger are stored empty. Drop the variable holding the oscillator into the second slot.
